newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece warns Albania over need for election deal.
newsitem.headline: Greece warns Albania over need for election deal.

text.p: Greece warned Albanian political parties on Tuesday that failure to reach a compromise for free and fair elections next month will put in doubt the presence of the multinational force guarding aid supplies.

"If the Albanian parties fail to reach agreement on the conditions under which the elections will be held, then we have a problem with the presence of the multinational force," Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos told a foreign press luncheon.

"The initiative (on the electoral law) by (Albanian President Sali) Berisha has endangered the path to elections. Nobody can use the multinational force to his advantage ... we did not go to Albania to promote separate political ambitions," he added.

The Albanian government warned on Tuesday of "unforeseen consequences" if a deal was not reached on the elections scheduled for June 29 and said Prime Minister Bashkim Fino had appealed to the West for help.
Despite marathon talks on Monday, Fino failed to persuade most parties to end a threatened boycott of elections in the volatile Balkan country.

"Although the debate continued all Monday, it failed not only to bring compromise or come near to compromise, but on the contrary took Albania to the edge of a deeper crisis with unforeseen consequences," Fino's office said in a statement.
Italy, leader of a multinational troop force safeguarding humanitarian aid, called on all political groups to make concessions.
"The next 24 hours are very important for the future of Albania," Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta told reporters in Rome.
Most parties of Fino's nine-party government say current election laws favour Berisha and his former ruling Democratic Party and want the laws changed.

The right-wing Democratic Party and its main rival, the Socialists, have been clashing for months over electoral rules. The Democrats favour more majority voting while the Socialists back more proportional representation.
Tsohatzopoulos said Fino had asked for the multinational force to have an increased mandate in Albania and along with the Western European Union help with the elections process.
"No decision has been taken on this matter yet," Tsohatzopoulos said.

Defence ministry officials said Greek troops, now stationed in Tirana, Vlore and Elbasan, may also be sent to the southern town of Gjirokaster and to abandoned customs offices in the border with Greece.
Former communist Albania plunged into anarchy and violence in February and March after thousands of people were left penniless by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.
Violence has subsided in recent weeks but some regions remain lawless. Nine people have been reported killed in gunfire since Sunday.
